clue.text: Great young Dickensian

parts.note: great in the sense of big and fat, as a great hulk of a man
a young person, a lad, is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone describes a promising youthful character from Dickens as great.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Boy is Joe, the sleepy, ever-eating page in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; 'Dickensian' here is a noun, a character from Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe, the gluttonous servant lad in The Pickwick Papers, is known as the Fat Boy, so he is a character from Dickens.

clue.text: Success on board deceives officer

parts.note: to fool someone is to deceive them
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A ship's officer is tricked aboard a vessel, which counts as a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means on the chessboard, not aboard ship: fool's mate is checkmate in two moves, the quickest win in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Fool's mate is the fastest possible checkmate, a quick win at chess.

clue.text: Used to wrong view about one being boring

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the letter for one
a mistaken view of the words used to gives them a different, wrong arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone once given to holding a wrong opinion turns out to be dull company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong view' scrambles USED TO into TEDOUS, which goes 'about' I to make TED-I-OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is wearisome and dull, so it bores those who must endure it.

clue.text: Habit theatre-goer got into

parts.note: habit here is clothing, as a monk's habit, not a custom: a garment that an evening patron of the opera house put on

explanation.surface: A custom that a playgoer fell into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' suggests a routine, but it means a garment, as in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera cloak is a long evening cape once worn over formal dress to the opera.

clue.text: Place money payable now

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
cash is ready money

explanation.surface: An instruction to put down money that is due immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot cash is money paid on delivery, at once, with no credit given.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash means immediate payment, money handed over on the spot rather than later.

clue.text: Proverbially far from dumb, the source of his power

definitions.text: Proverbially far from dumb, the source of his power

parts.words: Proverbially far from dumb, the source of his power
parts.note: the proverb says money talks, so the wealth that gives this rich ruler influence is anything but mute

explanation.surface: A powerful man's strength comes from something that famously can speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'money talks': money, far from dumb, is the source of a rich ruler's power.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone whose power derives from wealth, a member of a governing rich class.

clue.text: This match for Hampshire anglers?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this game suits fishermen in a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international cricket match; the River Test in Hampshire, an English county, is a famous trout and salmon stream for fly-fishing.

clue.text: Might be Juan in Hell

parts.note: Don Juan, the legendary libertine, could fairly be called a bad don, a wicked Spanish gentleman
don is the Spanish title for a gentleman, as in Don Juan

explanation.surface: A guess about whether a Spanish seducer has ended up in the inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend Don Juan is dragged down to hell for his sins; Abaddon, in the Bible, is the bottomless pit, or its angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaddon is a Hebrew name for the abyss or place of destruction, the underworld itself.

clue.text: Maybe loth to include eastern traveller's need

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are made to include the next piece inside them
maybe suggests the word loth could be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps reluctant to take in an Eastern requirement of someone on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' scrambles LOTH into HOTL, which 'to include' wraps round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is where a traveller finds a bed for the night, something someone on a journey requires.

clue.text: Geraint's love gets one finally, apparently

indicators.note: the closing word gets, or receives, the letter for one inside it

parts.note: the end comes finally, at the close
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A knight's sweetheart at last gains something, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' puts I inside END. In Tennyson's Idylls of the King, Enid is the wife of Geraint, a knight of the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is the faithful wife of Sir Geraint in Arthurian legend and Tennyson's Geraint and Enid.

clue.text: Familiar address given in Oban — led astray

indicators.note: something led astray is taken off its proper course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting heard in a Scottish port town, where someone was misled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led astray' rearranges OBAN and LED together. Oban is a west-coast Scottish town; 'old bean' is a dated, jovial British way of addressing a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Old bean' is a chummy British form of address between friends, like 'old chap'.

clue.text: This parvenu's U, apparently

parts.note: the letter U is what you get at the beginning of the little word up, so the clue's U is the opening of that word

explanation.surface: A social climber is described as U, the old label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' was 1950s slang for upper-class; a parvenu pretends to be U. Cryptically, U is the start of UP, i.e. UP'S START.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a newcomer to wealth or rank, someone who has risen suddenly and is resented for it.

clue.text: Walter to go round and look into old assessments

indicators.note: Walter's surname is made to encircle the following pieces, going round them

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, the Scottish novelist
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Scott sets out to investigate historical tax records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts AND LO inside SCOTT. Scot and lot was a medieval English municipal tax shared among householders.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot and lot was a tax levied on townspeople by their borough, an assessment for local dues in former times.

clue.text: Figure's one pound — about the same

indicators.note: the pound sign's letter sits around the next piece, going about it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
do, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: A number of one pound appears, roughly equal to before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DO (ditto) inside I and L, giving I-DO-L.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a statue or image worshipped as a god, a carved figure.

clue.text: Woman without spirit in Longfellow's poem

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the woman stands outside the next pieces

parts.note: Eve was the first woman
an angel is a heavenly spirit

explanation.surface: A woman who has lost her drink, or soul, appears in a Longfellow work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: EVE goes round ANGEL and IN. 'Woman' and 'spirit' suggest gin or soul, but EVE and ANGEL are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangeline is Longfellow's 1847 narrative poem about an Acadian girl separated from her betrothed.

clue.text: Pardon Jack's love of disorder

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman), so jack's gives AB's

indicators.note: the word love is put into disorder, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor confesses a fondness for messiness and asks to be excused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of disorder' scrambles LOVE into OLVE, which follows ABS.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to forgive or release someone from guilt, to grant a pardon.

clue.text: Team's diet must be varied, it is judged

indicators.note: the letters must be changed about into another order

parts.note: the word team's, with its s counting as a letter

explanation.surface: A sports side is told its food needs more variety, according to some assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be varied' rearranges TEAMS and DIET; 'it is' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimated means approximately calculated, roughly judged or assessed.

clue.text: Bird article returned from Italian city

parts.note: the raven is a large black bird

indicators.note: the article is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bird and some writing came back from a city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses AN to NA after RAVEN; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in Emilia-Romagna, northern Italy, famed for its Byzantine mosaics.

clue.text: Reptile bagged eventually, perhaps

parts.note: a large swamp creature whose skin may in time end up made into a fashionable handbag, so it might be bagged in more than one sense

explanation.surface: A hunter's quarry, a reptile, is finally captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagged' looks like a hunter's catch; the creature's hide is famously made into handbags.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large American reptile whose leather is prized for handbags and shoes.

clue.text: Passage from book contains more heartless cant

parts.note: extra means additional, more

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outer letters of cant remain

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a book is full of even more hollow hypocritical talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only CT, the first and last letters of 'cant', which follow EXTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short piece quoted or taken out of a longer written work.

clue.text: Some climb by Hudson's Bay man?

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upwards, so the word for some is read from bottom to top

parts.note: part means some, a portion
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A few people go climbing beside the Canadian bay named after Henry Hudson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' reverses PART to TRAP in this down clue. The Hudson's Bay Company traded furs bought from trappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappers caught animals for their furs and sold the pelts to the Hudson's Bay Company in Canada.

clue.text: This gives a lift to border climber

definitions.text: This gives a lift to border climber

parts.words: This gives a lift to border climber
parts.note: a climbing plant in a garden bed uses a thin coiling shoot to pull itself upwards, not a car lift for someone scaling a frontier

explanation.surface: Something offers a ride to a mountaineer at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' is the flower bed, not a frontier, and the 'climber' is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant grips a support and hauls itself up.

clue.text: Object in torn clothes

indicators.note: the goal word goes in, inside the word for torn

parts.note: rent means torn, ripped
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: Something sits inside ragged garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun for a thing; it is AIM, a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or dress.

clue.text: Rock government?

explanation.surface: A two-word note pairing geology with politics.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway is to rock from side to side; sway is also rule or dominion, as in holding sway over a land.

clue.text: Mark on forehead? It's round the neck

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
the head of fore is its first letter, F

explanation.surface: A blemish sits on someone's brow, while something wraps their throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forehead' is read as fore-head, the head (first letter) of 'fore'; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarf is a strip of cloth worn around the throat for warmth or show.

clue.text: Superficial knowledge of direction being of importance

parts.note: S stands for south, a compass direction
mattering means being significant or important

explanation.surface: A shallow understanding of which way is significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; S is south.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, surface acquaintance with a subject, only a little learning.

clue.text: Late Chinese money changer

indicators.note: a changer alters the four letters of late into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A deceased Chinese bureau de change clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changer' rearranges LATE; it hides in 'money changer', a phrase that suggests a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tael was a Chinese unit of weight for silver, used as a currency.

clue.text: Wood's prejudice?

explanation.surface: A question whether a forest has an unfair leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls a wood is a ball weighted to curve, its built-in lean called its bias; bias is also partiality or prejudice.

clue.text: Nominate composer of a piano score

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a point is a score in a game

explanation.surface: Name the person who wrote a piece of music for piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer of' looks like the musician but is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to name or choose someone for a post, as to nominate them.

clue.text: Result includes number one backed, that's obvious

indicators.note: the outcome word takes in the next pieces, including them inside

parts.note: an event is an outcome or result, as in 'in the event'

indicators.note: these two letters are put in reverse, backed up from right to left

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An outcome featuring the champion going into reverse is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns DI into ID, which 'includes' puts inside EVENT: EV-ID-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain and clearly seen, so it is plainly apparent to all.

clue.text: If to retire, live in warm place

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: A person plans retirement and living somewhere cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reverses IF to FI; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is the area beside the hearth, the cosiest spot in a house.

clue.text: Disturber of game is the prevailing type?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person who spoils a match is always the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A beater flushes grouse or pheasants from cover for the guns at a shoot; and one who beats others is a victor, one who prevails.
